title: Practice: sending coins
hook: Your friend asks you to send 50 practice coins to their wallet. They paste their [[address]] into a chat.
card1: An [[address]] is like an account number for a [[wallet]]. Anyone can send coins to it, but only the person with the [[private-key]] can move them out.
card2: Addresses are long and hard to read. Scammers use that: they change one character, or swap the address you copied for their own.
card3: Sending coins creates a [[transaction]]. You also pay a small [[fee]] to the network for processing it.
card4: Once a transaction is confirmed, it is [[irreversible]]. No bank can cancel it or give the coins back.

paste.prompt: Your friend's address has arrived in the chat. What do you do before you press Send?

type.label: Type the address by hand
type.before: You will retype the address yourself, one character at a time.
type.what: You typed one character wrong. Your 50 practice coins went to a different address and are gone for good.
type.why: Almost any string of the right length can be a valid address, so the network accepted it and delivered the coins.
type.how: No bank sits in the middle to check names or stop mistakes. The network only checks that the address has a valid format.
type.realLife: Never type an address by hand. Copy and paste it, then compare the first and last 4 characters with the original.
type.more: The wrong address may belong to someone, or to no one at all. Either way, without that address's [[private-key]] nobody can move the coins back to you.

send.label: Copy-paste it and send right away
send.before: You will paste the address and send without checking it.
send.what: The coins arrived this time. But you skipped the check that protects you from address-swapping malware.
send.why: Some malware watches what you copy and replaces a wallet address with the attacker's address.
send.how: A swapped address looks similar at a glance, so only comparing the characters reveals it.
send.realLife: After pasting, always compare the first and last 4 characters with the address your friend sent.

check.label: Copy-paste it, then check the first and last 4 characters
check.before: You will paste the address and compare its start and end with the original.
check.what: The characters match. Your 50 practice coins arrive safely in your friend's wallet.
check.why: Copy-paste avoids typing mistakes, and the check catches a swapped address.
check.how: A wrong address almost never shares both the first and the last 4 characters with the right one by chance.
check.realLife: For a large amount, send a small test amount first and ask your friend to confirm it arrived.

q1.prompt: You sent coins to the wrong address. What can you do?
q1.a: Ask an exchange or a bank to reverse it
q1.b: Nothing, unless the owner of that address sends them back
q1.c: Wait 24 hours and the coins return automatically
q1.explanation: A confirmed transaction is irreversible. Only the owner of the receiving address could send the coins back, and only if they choose to.

q2.prompt: What is the safest way to enter an address?
q2.b: Copy-paste it and check the first and last 4 characters
q2.c: Use the address a helpful stranger sends you in a DM
q2.explanation: Copy-paste avoids typing mistakes, and checking the start and end catches an address that was swapped.

misc.refund: Many people believe someone can reverse a payment. On a blockchain no one can: a confirmed transaction is final.
misc.autoReturn: Transactions do not expire or bounce back. If the address is valid, the coins stay there.
misc.carefulTyping: Even careful typing goes wrong sometimes, and one wrong character is enough to lose everything.
misc.trustDm: A stranger's address is where your coins would go. Helpful strangers in DMs are a classic scam.

t1: Never type an address by hand.
t2: After pasting, compare the first and last 4 characters.
t3: A confirmed transaction cannot be undone.
